statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds at 20% at the watch floor after initial jobless claims printed 197,000 against consensus near 200K and NQ absorbed the release without expanding its 30,684.50 to 31,147.75 session range, while Brent back above 100 dollars and the ISM manufacturing print still ahead keep Stress at 74%.
recommendation: Tail is unchanged at 20% and remains five points below the 25% block threshold. The decisive development is that the first catalyst in the danger window has cleared without producing structure. Initial jobless claims for the week ending 26 September printed 197,000 against consensus near 200K, a decrease of 1,000 from a prior week revised up to 198,000, with the four-week average at 200,000 and continuing claims at 1,701,000 against a 1,730K consensus, well below expectation. The observed reaction was negligible: NQ stood at 30,856.25 two minutes after the release against 30,856.75 shortly before it, the session range of 30,684.50 to 31,147.75 did not widen in either direction, no new extreme printed, and 10-year note futures ticked up 0.10% so the long end was marginally bid rather than sold. A high-impact labour print landing below consensus and generating no directional impulse is the clearest available evidence against the pathological path the Tail score measures, and it repeats the pattern recorded on 7 August, when a large payrolls shock did not become a no-retracement path. The wider structure agrees. A 463-point retracement from the 31,147.75 high to 30,684.50 was followed by a roughly 170-point recovery on volume expanding to about 161k contracts, with a second venue corroborating the level at 30,853.75; both Treasury maturities are lower on the day, the 2-year at 4.868% and the 10-year at 5.294%; VIX has eased to 16.29, near its 16.21 session low; and the intra-equity dispersion flagged in preceding assessments has closed, with Dow futures now up 0.30% at 51,433.00. There is no session-extreme holding, no shallow-pullback sequence and no repeated extension after a failed retracement. Stress eases a point to 74%, high rather than extreme, because one catalyst has cleared while Brent for December has reclaimed 100.03 dollars on a 2.0% gain as Chinese refiners suspend October fuel exports and Gulf supply stays about 3.2 million barrels per day below pre-conflict levels, against a 10-year still near multi-decade highs. The 12:00-15:00Z danger window is unchanged because its two largest remaining checkpoints, the 13:30Z cash open and ISM manufacturing at 14:00Z, are still ahead, and that is the range where an observed post-release continuation would justify escalation.
headline: Jobless claims print 197,000 below consensus and NQ absorbs it without widening its session range, holding Tail at 20% as both Treasury yields fall and VIX eases to 16.29 ahead of ISM manufacturing
body: December E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures trade near 30,856.25, up 157.50 points or 0.51% from the 30,698.75 settle, with a session range of 30,684.50 to 31,147.75 on about 161k contracts. A second independent venue corroborates the level at 30,853.75, so the price is well established. The defining event of this hour is that initial jobless claims have printed and been absorbed. The Department of Labor reported 197,000 advance seasonally adjusted initial claims for the week ending 26 September, a decrease of 1,000 from a previous week revised up from 197,000 to 198,000, against a consensus near 200K, with the four-week moving average falling 2,500 to 200,000. Continuing claims for the week ending 19 September came in at 1,701,000, down 11,000 from a downward-revised 1,712,000 and materially below a 1,730K consensus, with the insured unemployment rate unchanged at 1.1%. The labour market therefore remains tight, which in a regime where the market is still pricing the possibility of further tightening is a genuine rates channel. The observed response, however, was close to nil. NQ was 30,856.25 at a quote stamped two minutes after the release against 30,856.75 shortly before it; the session range did not widen at either end; no new high or low printed; and volume advanced only from about 158k to about 161k contracts. Ten-year note futures were 104.31, up 0.11 points or 0.10%, so the long end was marginally bid rather than sold into the print. This is orderly two-way price discovery through a high-impact release, and it is the structural opposite of what the Tail score is built to detect, namely directional efficiency on thinning participation with retracements that fail. The wider picture reinforces it. The 463 points of overnight advance given back to 30,684.50 have been followed by a roughly 170-point recovery, leaving price about 290 points below the overnight high and some 240 points below the 31,094.75 pivot that earlier assessments named as the marker of genuine uptrend resumption. Cross-asset confirmation has improved rather than deteriorated: the 2-year is 4.868% against a 4.887% close within a 4.858 to 4.920% range and the 10-year is 5.294% against a 5.311% close within a 5.272 to 5.362% range, so the rates impulse that drove yesterday's session has faded; VIX is 16.29, down 0.05 or 0.31%, near the 16.21 session low after a 17.00 high. Intra-equity dispersion, flagged previously as the one unresolved conflict, has closed, with Dow futures at 51,433.00, up 155.00 points or 0.30%, after being marginally negative an hour earlier, and S&P 500 futures at 7,744.00, up 0.37%. The advance is therefore broad rather than a narrow memory and semiconductor rotation, although that rotation remains its origin: Micron reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of 54.2 billion dollars and non-GAAP earnings of 33.42 dollars per share against a 31.83 dollar estimate, guided first-quarter revenue to 61.5 billion dollars, and described memory supply as constrained through calendar 2027 and 2028, while the stock itself is flat at 1,065.11 dollars. The clear offsetting pressure is energy. Brent for December has reclaimed 100.03 dollars on a 2.0% gain and WTI is near 91.59 to 92.37 dollars, driven by Chinese refiners suspending October fuel exports and by Gulf exports that, while recovering to 16.328 million barrels per day in September, remain about 3.2 million barrels per day below pre-conflict February levels. Iran has received a US response to its ceasefire proposal, so the geopolitical channel is genuinely two-sided and unresolved. That energy-led inflation impulse against a 10-year near multi-decade highs is what keeps Stress at 74%, in the high band, without implying a pathological price path. Confidence rises to 89%: the claims actuals come from the primary Department of Labor release, the live level is corroborated across two venues with a post-release timestamp, both yield points and VIX are current, oil and the China PMI backdrop are verified, and the seven-day calendar is confirmed. The remaining scheduled unknowns in the danger window are the 13:30Z cash open, the final manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z and ISM manufacturing at 14:00Z.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail entered the window at 20% in the 12:00Z hour of 30 September as the US data block and the long-end selloff developed, peaked at 23% around 15:00-16:00Z, and held 20-22% through the US afternoon and the early Asian session. It then firmed steadily from 20% at 00:00Z on 1 October through 21%, 22% and 23% to 24% at 05:00Z and 25% at 06:00Z, the only orange slot in the window, as NQ printed successive fresh overnight highs and accepted above the 31,094.75 pivot, with the mode turning trend-up across those two slots. The 07:00Z slot returned to 22% and the mixed mode once the first liquid two-way test produced a 188-point retracement, and 08:00Z through 11:00Z held the 20% watch floor as that retracement extended past 460 points on expanding turnover without producing any amplifier. Stress rose almost monotonically across the period from 70% to a 76% peak at 10:00Z before easing a point, and Confidence held 85-88% throughout.
outlookSummary: The danger window is unchanged at 12:00-15:00Z. Its first component has now cleared: initial claims printed 197,000 against consensus near 200K and continuing claims 1,701,000 against 1,730K, absorbed without any widening of the session range. Still ahead are the 13:30Z cash open, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z with consensus near 57.0, and ISM manufacturing plus August construction spending at 14:00Z with ISM consensus near 54.7 to 55.0 against a prior near 54.6. Forecast Tail holds the 20% watch floor in the current hour, firms to 22% across the cash open and final PMI and to a US-day peak of 23% in the 14:00Z ISM hour where Stress tops at 77%, then eases to 21-22% through the US afternoon as observed discovery replaces scheduled risk. It firms a point to 22% into the power hour and the 20:00Z cash close, then eases to 20-21% through the quiet post-close hours, where Stress reaches its forecast low of 71% and the mode turns normal. It firms again through the Asian session to 21-22%, reaches 23% across the European open and morning, and tops the watch band at 24% through the late European morning as positioning concentrates ahead of September non-farm payrolls at 12:30Z on 2 October, where Stress peaks at 78% in the final pre-release hour. No slot in the path reaches the 25% block threshold, because scheduled event importance, forecast dispersion and surprise magnitude are carried through Stress and Confidence rather than through Tail until an observed price path establishes mean-reversion failure. Confidence decays from 89% to 82% with forecast distance and recovers to 83-84% once European cash hours restore observable structure.
